label: Step right after a "0" input at position 1 or 2 of the original sequence
explanation: Fires during the original-input phase at step t=1 or t=2 exactly when the previous input was the digit 0, i.e. the original sequence starts with 0 (fires at t=1) or has 0 as its second token (fires at t=2). Dev: precision 1.0, recall 0.99. It is essentially silent when the 0 sits later in the sequence (t>=3), on the delimiter, and in the copy phase, even when a 0 is being re-fed or output. The current input token barely matters. Magnitude: mean activation is higher at t=1 (the 0 is the first token; 60% of mass from about half the firings) than at t=2. At t=2 the first token modulates strength: the global max comes from sequences starting with t (t 0 _), and weak activations from first tokens such as z, 3, e. There are tiny residual activations (<0.1 of max) at t=2 after a w input, and those carry no mass.

issues: The claims hold up. On the test split the predicate scores precision 1.0, recall 0.990, F1 0.995 and mass recall 0.9996, with 0 false positives.

All 358 test misses together carry 0.0% of the activation mass, and every one is at most 0.03 of max. They come from two tiny residual patterns. The first is step 2 after 't w' (prev_tok w, 261 steps on dev). The second is step 3 in sequences starting 'k v 0'. Both are negligible.
The phase claim checks out: 0 activations on the delimiter and 7 of 33,911 in the copy phase. The position claim also checks out: t=1 carries 0.598 of the mass, t=2 carries 0.401, and t>=3 carries 0.

The magnitude claims hold. The top activations are all 't 0 [p]' at 1.00. The low quartile includes first tokens z (0.37), 3 (0.58) and e (0.59). The t=1 firings (about half the count) hold 60% of the mass, so their mean activation is higher.
One small wording issue: the explanation says the misses come after a 'w input'. They actually occur specifically when the sequence starts 't w'. This is immaterial.
